screenInspector.title: Screen Properties
screenInspector.categoryHint: Editor-only label + color to tell screen kinds apart in the list. No effect on the game.
screenInspector.openHotkeyHint: A key that toggles this screen open/closed during gameplay (e.g. "I" for an inventory). Built-in keys (Space/Enter, H, Ctrl, Esc) take priority.
screenInspector.bgOpacityHint: 100% = solid. Lower it to let whatever is behind this screen show through.
screenInspector.gameHudHint: Always display this screen on top of gameplay (no command needed) — for a persistent status bar, button bar, or affection meters. Only one screen can be the game HUD.
screenInspector.hudNonBlockingHint: When this screen is opened with the Show Screen command, the story keeps playing behind it instead of freezing — for an HP bar or status overlay that updates as the game runs. Leave OFF for modal menus that should pause the scene until closed.
screenInspector.passThroughHint: When on, empty areas let clicks reach the scene/game beneath — only visible elements capture input. Recommended for the in-game HUD and item/drag overlays. The Game HUD screen defaults to on.
screenInspector.pauseSceneHint: Freeze the scene behind this screen while it's open (no auto-advance, skip, or clicking past). The scene stays visible but paused — ideal for an inventory or stats popup opened mid-dialogue.
screenInspector.onCloseHint: Controls what happens when this overlay closes. Default keeps today's behavior; Resume returns without advancing; Advance moves the story one step; Run actions fires the list below.
screenInspector.interactivityHint: Add a hot spot (a click or drop zone) or an interactive element — a draggable, clickable image, Interactive Image, button, or text. Pick its kind and behaviour in the inspector.
screenInspector.layerDepthHint: Layer orders the backdrop vs. elements; Depth drives parallax (set a Parallax mode below).
screenInspector.additionalBgsHint: Extra backdrop planes layered with the main background — give each its own layer + depth for parallax scrolling.
screenInspector.hudAboveDialogueHint: Renders this HUD overlay on top of the dialogue box and choices so players can open and interact with it mid-dialogue. Empty areas still pass clicks through to advance.
screenInspector.parallaxHint: Shifts the background + elements by their Depth for a sense of depth. Set per-element depth in the element's Transform group.
screenInspector.parallaxCameraNote: Screens have no camera (Pan/Zoom is a scene feature), so Camera mode has no effect here — use Follow mouse.
screenInspector.spotlightIntensityHint: The strength slider sets how dark the rest of the screen goes behind the beams.
screenInspector.lightsIntensityHint: The strength slider is a master brightness for all the lights — bind it to a variable to dim them in play.
screenInspector.showBeneathHint: When this screen opens on top of another (or the game HUD), the one beneath stays visible under it — like a popup. Great for an inventory or map opened from a button. Tip: give this screen a see-through background so the screen underneath shows. Off = this screen replaces the previous one.

sceneTransitions.title: Scene Transitions
sceneTransitions.intro: Your own scene-change animations — like a theatre curtain. The closing animation covers the screen, the scene switches while it’s covered, then the opening animation reveals the new scene. Pick one in a scene’s Scene Settings, or on a single Jump / choice.
sceneTransitions.empty: None yet. Click “New” to make one.
sceneTransitions.name: Name
sceneTransitions.closingHint: Plays over the current scene. Its final image should cover the whole screen — that’s when the scene switches.
sceneTransitions.openingHint: Plays over the new scene, revealing it. Its first image should cover the whole screen; its last should show the scene fully.
sceneTransitions.oneFileHint: An animated PNG / animated WebP / GIF set to play once, or a video. It stays on its final image when it finishes.
sceneTransitions.halfDurationHint: Set this to match the animation’s own length.
sceneTransitions.noFrames: No frames yet — add your images in play order.
sceneTransitions.sequenceLength: Plays for about {{seconds}}s, then holds the last frame.
